note: A user reported a 16-minute recipe video producing a document with almost no photos. It is not an outlier: guide production barely scales with video length, so long videos get a near-constant handful of guides spread over many more steps.

corpus.source: ko holdout + en holdout + rerun-2 analyses

finding: Guides per minute collapses from 2.32 (under 3 min) to 0.13 (over 20 min) while median steps rise 3 -> 7, so coverage falls 59% -> 37%. The model emits a roughly fixed number of guides regardless of how much content there is.

chunked_analysis_probe.method: Gemini accepts video_metadata start/end offsets on YouTube file_uri parts, and the timestamps it returns are absolute (verified), so per-segment analysis is safe.
chunked_analysis_probe.verdict: More guides (4.8 -> 6.8) but coverage did NOT improve (50% -> 45%) because chunking also fragments steps (7 -> 12). Not yet compared against spending the same call budget on whole-video passes, which is the fair control — that comparison is the open question, deliberately left unrun.
